'''Priya Bapat''' (born 18 September 1986) is an Indian actress who works in [[Marathi language|Marathi]] and [[Hindi]] films, television, theatre and web series.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-09-08 |title=While OTT is a blessing, the struggle never ends: Priya Bapat |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/bollywood/news/while-ott-is-a-blessing-the-struggle-never-ends-priya-bapat/articleshow/123759787.cms |access-date=2025-09-21 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> Known for her versatility across genres, she has received several accolades including two [[Maharashtra State Film Awards]] and a [[Zee Chitra Gaurav Puraskar]], in addition to multiple nominations at Filmfare Marathi and other ceremonies.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Top 5 Actresses:सर्वात जास्त मानधन घेणाऱ्या मराठी अभिनेत्री कोण माहितीये काय? |url=https://www.esakal.com/image-story/know-highly-paid-top-five-actresses-in-marathi-film-industrypriya-bapatsai-tamhankarsonali-kulkarniamruta-khanvilkarsrr99 |access-date=2023-06-19 |website=eSakal - Marathi Newspaper |language=mr-IN |archive-date=25 January 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240125134259/https://www.esakal.com/image-story/know-highly-paid-top-five-actresses-in-marathi-film-industrypriya-bapatsai-tamhankarsonali-kulkarniamruta-khanvilkarsrr99 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2018-07-26 |title=Priya Bapat: The actress's movies you should not miss |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/marathi/photo-features/priya-bapat-the-actresss-movies-you-should-not-miss/photostory/65150483.cms |access-date=2025-09-21 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

Bapat began her career as child artist with television dramas and the films such as ''[[Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar (film)|Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar]]'' (2000) and ''[[Munna Bhai M.B.B.S.]]'' (2003), before gaining prominence with the Marathi blockbuster ''[[Mi Shivajiraje Bhosale Boltoy!]]'' (2009). Bapat established herself with acclaimed performances in the period drama ''[[Kaksparsh]]'' (2012), the drama ''[[Happy Journey (2014 Marathi film)|Happy Journey]]'' (2014), the slice of life ''[[Vazandar]]'' (2016), the phycological drama ''Pimpal'' (2017), and the feminist drama ''[[Aamhi Doghi]]'' (2018).

Beyond films, Bapat has been active in theatre with plays like ''Nava Gadi Nava Rajya'' and ''Jar Tar Chi Goshta'', and has found success in digital media her portrayal of Poornima Gaikwad in ''[[City of Dreams (TV series)|City of Dreams]]'' (2019–2023), which won her several awards and emerged as a defining role. She has also appeared in Hindi films including ''Chakki'' (2022), ''[[Visfot]]'' (2024) and ''[[Costao]]'' (2025).

In addition to acting, Bapat has engaged in entrepreneurial ventures, co-founding a clothing label with her sister. She married actor [[Umesh Kamat]] in 2011, with whom she frequently collaborates on stage and screen.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-06-02 |title=Priya and I have each other's back: Umesh Kamat |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/regional-movies/priya-and-i-have-each-other-s-back-umesh-kamat/story-ut7bqMEygm7EON0tbqMKZO.html |access-date=2025-09-21 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Priya Bapat was born on 18 September 1986 in [[Mumbai]], [[Maharashtra]], to Sharad and Smita Bapat.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Priya Bapat Is All Praise For Her Mother's Fearless Nature In This Adorable Post |url=https://www.news18.com/news/movies/priya-bapat-is-all-praise-for-her-mothers-fearless-nature-in-this-adorable-post-5141815.html |access-date=2025-08-27 |website=News18 |language=en}}</ref> She was raised in [[Dadar]], where she spent her childhood in a chawl on Ranade Road.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-07-15 |title=Did you know 'Munna Bhai MBBS' actor Priya Bapat reveals she lived in a chawl for 25 years even after her Bollywood debut? |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/bollywood/news/did-you-know-munna-bhai-mbbs-actor-priya-bapat-reveals-she-lived-in-a-chawl-for-25-years-even-after-her-bollywood-debut/articleshow/101754247.cms |access-date=2025-08-27 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2018-05-10 |title=Exclusive: This popular actress spent her 25 years at a chawl in Dadar, read to know who? |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/tv/news/marathi/exclusive-this-popular-actress-spent-her-25-years-at-a-chawl-in-dadar-read-to-know-who/articleshow/64106759.cms |access-date=2025-08-27 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

Bapat studied at Balmohan Vidyamandir, where she developed a keen interest in the performing arts and regularly participated in plays, dramas, and talent competitions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marathi Movie Actress Priya Bapat Biography, News, Photos, Videos |url=https://nettv4u.com/celebrity/marathi/movie-actress/priya-bapat |access-date=2025-08-27 |website=nettv4u |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-11-26 |title=On a ROLL! - Pune Times Mirror |url=https://punemirror.com/specials/fab-champs/on-a-roll/ |access-date=2025-08-27 |language=en-US}}</ref> She received training in [[Indian classical music|classical music]] under Shubhada Dadarkar for two years, with a focus on devotional songs and later trained under vocalist Uttara Kelkar, though she eventually discontinued due to vocal cord issues.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2018-09-18 |title=Priya Bapat: Interesting facts about the Marathi actress |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/marathi/movies/news/priya-bapat-interesting-facts-about-the-marathi-actress/photostory/65857704.cms?picid=65857799 |access-date=2025-08-27 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> After finishing school, Bapat pursued a [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree in [[Economics]] and subsequently earned a Bachelor’s degree in [[Mass communication|Mass Communication]] from [[Ramnarain Ruia College]], [[Matunga]]. During her time in college, she also completed a short course in filmmaking.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-31 |title=Meet actress who faced 100 rejections, then made hit debut with Sanjay Dutt; still lived in chawl for years |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/bollywood/meet-priya-bapat-who-faced-100-rejections-then-made-hit-debut-with-sanjay-dutt-still-lived-in-chawl-for-25-years-101735639886556.html |access-date=2025-08-27 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==

=== Child artist and early recognition (2000–2010) ===
Priya Bapat stepped into acting as a child artist, appearing in the acclaimed Marathi television shows ''Damini'' (2000), ''Bandini'' (2000), ''De Dhamal'' (2001), and in the theatre production ''Vatevaratee Kaachaa Ga''.<ref>{{cite web |date=2025-07-14 |title=Do you remember the popular serial “De Dhamal” of the '90s? Child actors are difficult to recognize now |url=https://www.lokmat.com/filmy/photos/television/do-you-remember-the-popular-serial-de-dhamaal-of-the-90s-child-actors-are-difficult-to-recognize-now-a-a603/ |access-date=2025-08-15 |website=Lokmat}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Marathi Tv Serial Bandini Marathi Synopsis Aired On DD sahyadri Channel |url=https://nettv4u.com/about/marathi/tv-serials/bandini-marathi |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=nettv4u |language=en}}</ref> Her film debut came the same year with [[Jabbar Patel]]’s National Award-winning biographical drama ''[[Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar (film)|Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar]]'' (2000), where she played young [[Ramabai Bhimrao Ambedkar|Ramabai Ambedkar]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ramnath |first=Nandini |date=2019-05-26 |title=Priya Bapat is a star on the Marathi screen – but here is why she isn't resting on her laurels |url=https://scroll.in/reel/924675/priya-bapat-is-a-star-on-the-marathi-screen-but-here-is-why-she-isnt-resting-on-her-laurels |access-date=2025-09-07 |website=Scroll.in |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-31 |title=Meet actress who faced 100 rejections, then made hit debut with Sanjay Dutt; still lived in chawl for years |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/bollywood/meet-priya-bapat-who-faced-100-rejections-then-made-hit-debut-with-sanjay-dutt-still-lived-in-chawl-for-25-years-101735639886556.html |access-date=2025-09-07 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref>

She next featured as a child actor in [[Chandrakant Kulkarni]]’s ''[[Bhet]]'' (2002).<ref>{{cite news|date=2002-06-18|title=Hedging his bhets|url=http://archive.mid-day.com/entertainment/2002/jun/25793.htm|work=[[Mid-day]]|language=en-IN|publication-place=[[Mumbai|Mumbai, India]]|publisher=Mid-Day Infomedia|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191213130950/http://archive.mid-day.com/entertainment/2002/jun/25793.htm|archive-date=2019-12-13|access-date=2025-08-15}}</ref> Bapat later grabbed attention in Bollywood through brief but notable appearances in [[Rajkumar Hirani]]’s ''[[Munna Bhai M.B.B.S.]]'' (2003) and its sequel ''[[Lage Raho Munna Bhai]]'' (2006), both starring [[Sanjay Dutt]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dwivedie |first=Jaya |last2=Hindi |first2=India TV |date=2025-02-27 |title='मुन्ना भाई MBBS' वाली ये लड़की याद है? चॉल में काटे 25 साल, अब बनी OTT स्टार |url=https://www.indiatv.in/entertainment/ott/munna-bhai-mbbs-actress-priya-bapat-spent-25-years-in-chawl-now-become-ott-star-and-changed-her-life-2025-02-27-1116338 |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=India TV Hindi |language=hi}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-09-07 |title=Marathi actor Priya Bapat says she has never faced prejudices in Bollywood |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/entertainment/web-series/marathi-actor-priya-bapat-says-she-has-never-faced-prejudices-in-bollywood-101631028594839.html |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref> Recalling her audition, she once said, "I went to Hirani's office. I auditioned and I got the part. It was that simple."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Priya Bapat On Playing Medical Student In Munna Bhai M.B.B.S: 'I Was So Naive…' |url=https://www.news18.com/movies/priya-bapat-on-playing-medical-student-in-munna-bhai-m-b-b-s-i-was-so-naive-8017591.html |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=News18 |language=en}}</ref> Between 2004 and 2006, she made a mark on television with ''[[Adhuri Ek Kahani]]'', playing a spirited role opposite established actors like [[Swapnil Joshi]], [[Kishori Godbole]] and [[Neena Kulkarni]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2020-09-23 |title=Swwapnil Joshi recalls 'Adhuri Ek Kahaani' memories; shares throwback picture with Kishori Godbole |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/tv/news/marathi/swwapnil-joshi-recalls-adhuri-ek-kahaani-memories-shares-throwback-picture-with-kishori-godbole/articleshow/78271397.cms |access-date=2025-09-16 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> Her energy on screen was widely appreciated.<ref>{{Cite web |last=जोशी |first=मानसी |date=2022-09-14 |title=अधुरी एक कहाणी (Adhuri Ek Kahani): नात्यांची गुंतागुंत आणि थोडंसं रहस्य असणारी कौटुंबिक मालिका |url=https://kalakrutimedia.com/memories-of-marathi-serial-adhuri-ek-kahani/ |access-date=2025-09-16 |website=Kalakruti Media |language=en-US}}</ref>

Her transition into lead roles began in 2009 with ''[[Mi Shivajiraje Bhosale Boltoy!]]'', a story highlighting an underdog’s struggle against social ills.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marathi film beats Hindi movies - Behindwoods.com - Hindi Movie News - Shivajiraje Bhosale Boltoy Chhabria Santosh Manjrekar |url=http://www.behindwoods.com/bollywood/hindi-movies-news/may-09-01/shivajiraje-bhosale-07-05-09.html |access-date=2025-09-17 |website=www.behindwoods.com}}</ref> Playing an aspiring actress struggling against stereotypes about Marathi women, she starred opposite [[Sachin Khedekar]], [[Suchitra Bandekar]] and [[Mahesh Manjrekar]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Editorial |first=M. Shantaram Annual Film Award nomination for Best Debut Artiste in a Leading Role. In 2010, she appeared in [[Zee Marathi]]’s ''Shubham Karoti'', which explored the complexities of a joint family,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marathi Tv Serial Shubham Karoti Synopsis Aired On Zee Marathi Channel |url=https://nettv4u.com/about/marathi/tv-serials/shubham-karoti |access-date=2025-09-17 |website=nettv4u |language=en}}</ref> She simultaneously took on roles in films such as Anandi Anand and Aika Dajiba alongside veterans like [[Vikram Gokhale]], [[Ashok Saraf]], [[Suhas Joshi]], [[Mohan Joshi]] and [[Vandana Gupte]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Panchal |first=Chetana Gavkhadkar |date=2010-05-07 |title=Marathi Film Anandi Anand Review |url=https://marathimovieworld.com/review/anandi-anand-review.php |access-date=2025-09-17 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="pearlriseentertainment.blogspot.com">{{Cite web |title=Movie Aika Dajiba on the floor very soon |url=http://pearlriseentertainment.blogspot.com/2010/08/movie-aika-dajiba-on-floor-very-soon.html |access-date=2025-09-17 |language=en}}</ref>

=== Breakthrough and acclaimed performances (2011–2018) ===
Bapat transitioned back to theatre, starring opposite [[Umesh Kamat]] in ''Nava Gadi Nava Rajya'' in the 2011, a stage play later adapted into [[Gujarati language|Gujarati]] and [[Konkani language|Konkani]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NAVA GADEE NAVA RAJYA Marathi Play/Drama - www.MumbaiTheatreGuide.com |url=https://www.mumbaitheatreguide.com/dramas/marathi/11-marathi-play-preview-nava-gaadi-nava-rajya.asp# |access-date=2025-09-17 |website=www.mumbaitheatreguide.com}}</ref> The story of a newlywed couple’s emotional journey resonated with audiences, and critics admired the duo’s chemistry.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2017-01-13 |title=Nava Gadi Nava Rajya adapted in Konkani |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/marathi/movies/news/nava-gadi-nava-rajya-adapted-in-konkani/articleshow/45165379.cms |access-date=2025-09-17 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref> Ambarish Ganesh of ''Indian Nerve'' wrote that “Bapat as the childlike Amruta steals hearts”.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nava Gadi Nava Rajya {{!}} Drama Review |url=https://indiannerve.com/nava-gadi-nava-rajya-drama-review-1443/ |access-date=2025-09-17 |website=Indian Nerve |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
She has an elder sister, Shweta Bapat, a [[costume designer]].

Bapat first met actor [[Umesh Kamat]] while she was in the 10th grade, at the premiere of ''[[Bhet]]'' (2002), but it was on the last day of shooting for the Marathi television series ''[[Aabhalmaya]]'' that the two exchanged numbers, which initiated their relationship.<ref>{{Cite web |title=How I Met My Life Partner: Priya Bapat Gushes, 'I Couldn't Take My Eyes Off Umesh When I First Saw Him' |url=https://www.freepressjournal.in/entertainment/how-i-met-my-life-partner-priya-bapat-gushes-i-couldnt-take-my-eyes-off-umesh-when-i-first-saw-him |access-date=2025-09-07 |website=Free Press Journal |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-06-24 |title=Power couple: Priya Bapat and Umesh Kamat |url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/regional-movies/power-couple-priya-bapat-and-umesh-kamat/story-BQ65gy6ltnNH4Ymvni6E0M.html |access-date=2025-09-07 |website=Hindustan Times |language=en}}</ref> After dating for nearly eight years, Bapat married Kamat on 5 October 2011 in a traditional Marathi wedding ceremony.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2021-10-06 |title=Priya Bapat and Umesh Kamat wedding anniversary: THESE photos prove that they are the coolest couple in the Marathi industry |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/marathi/movies/news/priya-bapat-and-umesh-kamat-wedding-anniversary-these-photos-prove-that-they-are-the-coolest-couple-in-the-marathi-industry/photostory/86805113.cms |access-date=2025-09-07 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |title=Priya Bapat and Umesh Kamat's unseen wedding pictures |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/videos/entertainment/regional/marathi/Priya-Bapat-and-Umesh-Kamats-unseen-wedding-pictures/videoshow/45262887.cms |access-date=2017-01-09}}</ref>

Priya Bapat (born 18 September 1986) is an Indian actress who works in Marathi and Hindi films, television, theatre and web series. Known for her versatility across genres, she has received several accolades including two Maharashtra State Film Awards and a Zee Chitra Gaurav Puraskar, in addition to multiple nominations at Filmfare Marathi and other ceremonies.
Bapat began her career as child artist with television dramas and the films such as Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar (2000) and Munna Bhai M.B.B.S. (2003), before gaining prominence with the Marathi blockbuster Mi Shivajiraje Bhosale Boltoy! (2009). Bapat established herself with acclaimed performances in the period drama Kaksparsh (2012), the drama Happy Journey (2014), the slice of life Vazandar (2016), the phycological drama Pimpal (2017), and the feminist drama Aamhi Doghi (2018).
Beyond films, Bapat has been active in theatre with plays like Nava Gadi Nava Rajya and Jar Tar Chi Goshta, and has found success in digital media her portrayal of Poornima Gaikwad in City of Dreams (2019–2023), which won her several awards and emerged as a defining role. She has also appeared in Hindi films including Chakki (2022), Visfot (2024) and Costao (2025).
In addition to acting, Bapat has engaged in entrepreneurial ventures, co-founding a clothing label with her sister. She married actor Umesh Kamat in 2011, with whom she frequently collaborates on stage and screen.
